To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electronic structure of tetragonal Cr-As, with a reduced longitudinal lattice constant, is more compatible to that of GaAs than the fcc structure.
(a) CrAs/GaAS heterostructures are likely candidates for efficient spin-filtering devices, and (b) half-metallic CrAs no longer seems to be a key ingredient for efficient spin-filter devices.

(i) the band alignment at the GaAs/CrAS interface is spin-dependent, (ii) the spin-dependent tunnel current in GaAs/CrAss/GaAs heterostuctures is large and (iii) these heterostructures can be used as room-temperature all semiconductor spin-filtering devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electronic structure of bulk and low-dimensional CrAs and CrAs/Gas heterostructures and its impact on spin-dependent transport properties.
the theoretical investigation of spin-filter devices based on the half-metal CrAs.
the electronic structure of bulk CrAs and the band alignment of CrAs/Ga As heterostructures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spin-filtering effect in CrAs/GaAS heterostructures is not due to half-metallic behavior of CrAs.
CrAs/GaAS heterostructures are promising candidates to be used in room temperature all-semiconductor spin filtering devices.
the spin-filtering effect is not only a property of half-metallic ferromagnets but can also be achieved with ferromagnets with a spin-polarized gap in the minority band.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CrAs is a promising material for spin-filtering applications.
the spin-filtering properties of CrAs/GaAS heterostructures are determined by the band offset and not by the half-metallicity of bulk CrAs.
the band alignment at the CrAs/GaAS interface is crucial for efficient spin-filtering.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spin-dependent tunneling can be realized without the need for half-metallicity, which is a very desirable property for future spintronic devices.
the spin-filtering properties of a CrAs/GaS heterostructure can be understood and designed from first principles, without the need for half-metallicity.
the electronic structure of the interface is the key to spin filtering in CrAs /GaAs heterostructures.
